Subject: MAP: embeddings + reranker benchmarking plan (proposal)

Hi Sara / Acme eng team —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our MAP kickoff, attached is a proposed evaluation plan focused on the two critical endpoints you identified: the embeddings service (for semantic search) and the reranker endpoint (for top-K re-scoring). High level goals: validate latency/throughput targets for production traffic, identify scale points for Dedicated capacity, and provide a quantifiable close recommendation tied to POC SLAs.

Summary of proposed benchmarks (short):
- Workload: 50k representative queries (mix of short/medium prompts) and 10k re-ranking requests constructed from your sample hits.
- Concurrency targets: 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100 concurrent clients.
- QPS targets: 50 / 100 / 150 sustained; short bursts to 300 qps for stress checks.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), TTFT (time to first token/ms), end-to-end throughput (queries/sec), successful response rate, and median tokens per response for embeddings and reranker.
- Cache/priming: warm vs cold cache runs; measure prefix cache hit impact.
- Test harness: locust for orchestration, wrk for microbenchmarks, and our internal trace capture for token-level TTFT.
- Environment: hosted Redwood dev cluster (g4dn-like) + option to repeat on Dedicated nodes (A100-sim) to compare.

Deliverables and timeline suggestion:
- Feb 11–12: Runner setup + dry-run on small sample (we'll need a test API key and a sample of 5k queries)
- Feb 12–13: Full runs and aggregation of results; produce CSV and annotated charts
- Feb 13: Share preliminary results + recommended config for POC (batching, quantization profile, and concurrency knobs)

Action items for you: please confirm the test API key user and whether we should operate under your VPC IP allowlist for the runs. I'm attaching a draft MAP spreadsheet with the milestones and acceptance criteria (Acme_MAP_v1.xlsx).

If anything above looks off, call it out and we'll adjust. Our aim is to make the MAP concrete so procurement and engineering have a clear sign-off path.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Internal: run notes + preliminary eval results (embeddings + reranker)

Quick internal update — I ran the orchestrated suite against Acme's sample set on our dev cluster. Summary of key numbers (cold start excluded; warm-cache runs unless noted):

Embeddings endpoint (model: open-embedding-v1, 1536-dim)
- 50 qps: p50 18 ms, p95 54 ms, p99 120 ms, TTFT median 6 ms
- 100 qps: p50 24 ms, p95 76 ms, p99 180 ms, sustained for 10 minutes without errors
- 150 qps: p50 44 ms, p95 210 ms, significant queueing after 3 minutes on shared dev nodes
- Burst behavior to 300 qps produced amplified p99 > 600 ms and ~1.4% error rate (timeouts)

Reranker endpoint (model: rerank-small-v2, sequence length avg 64 tokens)
- 25 qps: p50 32 ms, p95 98 ms, p99 240 ms, TTFT median 12 ms
- 50 qps: p50 45 ms, p95 210 ms, p99 480 ms, CPU-bound during ranking phase (noticed CPU saturation on the pre/post-processing container)
- 100 qps: sustained not achievable on dev nodes; observed queue growth and increased tail latency

Notes / interpretation:
- Embeddings scale well until ~100 qps on this hardware; beyond that you either need Dedicated nodes (higher GPU memory/compute) or aggressive batching/quantization.
- Reranker is more sensitive to CPU preprocessing and tokenization overhead; we should test colocating the preproc on the same GPU host and increasing fast-path batching.
- TTFT is low for both endpoints (single-digit ms for embeddings, ~10-12ms for reranker) — most tail is queuing.

Attachments produced: eval_results_20260212.csv (raw metrics), reranker_latency_trace.log (trace capture).

Recommendation for MAP milestone:
- Target POC acceptance: embeddings p95 <= 120ms at 100 qps; reranker p95 <= 300ms at 50 qps.
- If Acme needs 150 qps for embeddings, schedule Dedicated trial (we can reproduce those numbers with reserved capacity and recommended config).

Will prepare a one-page summary for external share.

- Stephanie
